source_title: Cyclone Arnab: Odisha prepares to airlift people stranded by floodwater
source_excerpt: BHUBANESWAR Roads were cut off and hundreds of villages inundated by floodwaters in Odisha’s Ganjam and Gajapati districts as the State government prepared to airlift people stranded by the deluge on Thursday (October 29, 2026). Union Home Minister Amit Shah spoke to Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi to enquire about the situation following the weakening of Cyclonic Storm Arnab. Follow Cyclone Arnab LIVE updates on October 29 https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/cyclone-arnab-weakens-into-depression-imd-alert-odisha-andhra-pradesh-telangana-live-updates-october-29-2026/article71638778.ece “We have been informed that around 2,000 people have been marooned in Ganjam district, with floodwaters cutting them off from all sides. The district collector is on the ground monitoring rescue operations. We are in constant touch with the Ministry of Home Affairs,” State Chief Secretary Anu Garg said. Ms. Garg said the Indian Coast Guard was on standby with rescue helicopters. However, persistent rain and low-hanging clouds were hampering aerial operations. Meanwhile, teams of the Odisha Disaster Rapid Action Force (ODRAF) were working to rescue as many stranded people as possible. Sources said the administration was prioritising the immediate airlifting of around 100 villagers from Sanakhemundi, Asika and the Gopalpur area of Ganjam district. G. Udayagiri in Kandhamal district and Mahendragarh in Gajapati district also recorded more than 400 mm of rainfall during the period. Three locations in central and southern Odisha recorded rainfall exceeding 300 mm, while eight others received more than 200 mm. The cyclonic storm triggered widespread rainfall across southern and southwestern Odisha. More than 200 villages in 22 blocks across Ganjam and Gajapati districts were severely affected. The State government deployed 15 additional ODRAF units to Ganjam to intensify rescue and relief operations. Road infrastructure also suffered extensive damage in Gajapati district. The hilly terrain compounded the situation, as torrents of rainwater rushed downhill into low-lying areas, triggering minor landslides and damaging infrastructure. Floodwaters were flowing over major roads at several locations, halting vehicular movement in the two districts. The floods also damaged paddy crops nearing harvest in parts of southern Odisha, dealing a blow to farmers, besides disrupting normal life and transport.
